## 2. Which indicators can run

*Joint coverage* = share of awards where **every** field the indicator needs is usable (value > 0 and KES, supplier ID present, and so on). Rule from SPEC 3.2: at least 60%.

| Indicator | Pref | Needs (usable) | Joint coverage | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `repeat_winner` | 1 | value, supplier_id | 80% | **runnable** |
| `value_outlier` | 2 | value, category | 99% | **runnable** |
| `single_bidder` | 3 | tenderers, method | 0% | not runnable |
| `non_competitive_share` | 3 | method, value | 99% | **runnable** |
| `short_window` | 3 | window | 82% | **runnable** |
| `date_sequence` | 3 | sequence | 81% | **runnable** |

## 3. Which date should `--from/--to` use?

Awards carry no date of their own. Candidates, with how often each is present and plausible:

| Field | Plausible | 2019 | 2020 | 2021 | 2022 | 2023 | 2024 | 2025 | 2026 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tenderPeriod.endDate` | 100% | 14 | 64 | 949 | 5,488 | 24,004 | 21,406 | 5,549 | 21 |
| `contract.dateSigned` | 81% | 123 | 86 | 887 | 5,848 | 25,664 | 14,096 | 8,000 | 505 |
| `award.contractPeriod.startDate` | 75% | 96 | 47 | 343 | 1,570 | 13,509 | 27,242 | 8,028 | 512 |

`tenderPeriod.startDate` is not a candidate: it is after `endDate` in 17% of processes (start <= end holds for 83%).

### Tender window length (end minus start, where start <= end)

| Days | Processes | % |
|---|---|---|
| 0-6 | 43,164 | 91% |
| 7-13 | 1,424 | 3% |
| 14-27 | 482 | 1% |
| 28+ | 2,553 | 5% |

Most windows are under a week, so `startDate` does not look like a real opening date and `short_window` would flag almost every process.
